description: New York's COVID-19 mitigation: schools closed from March 16 and the state paused non essential business on March 22; weekday demand ran 11 to 14 percent under temperature comparable demand through April
citation: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy, 6 May 2020, Daily electricity demand in New York falls about 13% after COVID-19 mitigation efforts, https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=43635

description: The central region's COVID-19 mitigation: the automotive plants announced closures on March 18 and demand ran 9 to 13 percent under temperature comparable demand from late March through April
citation: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy, 7 May 2020, Daily electricity demand impacts from COVID-19 mitigation efforts differ by region, https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=43636

description: Winter Storm Uri: ERCOT ordered firm load shed from 1:20 a.m. Central on February 15 and shed up to 20 GW; the demand the feed reports is what was served, well below what was wanted, until the shed ended late on February 18
citation: FERC, NERC and Regional Entity Staff Report, 8 December 2021, The February 2021 Cold Weather Outages in Texas and the South Central United States, https://www.ferc.gov/media/february-2021-cold-weather-outages-texas-and-south-central-united-states-ferc-nerc-and

description: Hurricane Ida made landfall in Louisiana at 11:55 a.m. Central on August 29; Entergy lost 210 transmission lines and hourly load in MISO's South region on August 30 was 25 to 30 percent below the average of the preceding days
citation: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy, 14 September 2021, Electric load in southern MISO fell as Hurricane Ida moved through Louisiana, https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=49536

description: The same event seen at the whole of MISO, where the South region is about a fifth of demand; listed so the page can say whether an authority level detector sees a regional collapse
citation: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy, 14 September 2021, Electric load in southern MISO fell as Hurricane Ida moved through Louisiana, https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=49536

description: Winter Storm Elliott: with over 6,000 MW of unplanned generation outages TVA ordered firm load shed of over 1,500 MW at 10:31 a.m. Eastern on December 23 and shed again, ten percent of its peak, early on December 24
citation: FERC, NERC and Regional Entity Staff Report, 7 November 2023, Inquiry into Bulk-Power System Operations During December 2022 Winter Storm Elliott, https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2023-11/24_Winter-Storm_Elliot_1107_1300.pdf

description: Winter Storm Elliott: Duke Energy Carolinas shed about 1,000 MW of firm load in rotating outages from the morning of December 24, about 500,000 customers across the Carolinas
citation: FERC, NERC and Regional Entity Staff Report, 7 November 2023, Inquiry into Bulk-Power System Operations During December 2022 Winter Storm Elliott, https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2023-11/24_Winter-Storm_Elliot_1107_1300.pdf

description: Winter Storm Elliott: Duke Energy Progress East shed about 961 MW of firm load in rotating outages on the morning of December 24
citation: FERC, NERC and Regional Entity Staff Report, 7 November 2023, Inquiry into Bulk-Power System Operations During December 2022 Winter Storm Elliott, https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2023-11/24_Winter-Storm_Elliot_1107_1300.pdf

description: Hurricane Beryl made landfall near Matagorda at about 4 a.m. Central on July 8 and cut power to about 2.2 million CenterPoint customers in Houston, most of ERCOT's Coast zone; ERCOT's forecast peak that day was about 20 percent below the same day's five year average
citation: S&P Global Commodity Insights, 8 July 2024, Hurricane Beryl lands on northern Texas Gulf Coast, cutting power to almost 1.8 million, https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/electric-power/070824-hurricane-beryl-lands-on-northern-texas-gulf-coast-cutting-power-to-almost-18-mil

description: The same event seen at the whole of ERCOT, where the Coast zone is about a quarter of demand
citation: S&P Global Commodity Insights, 8 July 2024, Hurricane Beryl lands on northern Texas Gulf Coast, cutting power to almost 1.8 million, https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/electric-power/070824-hurricane-beryl-lands-on-northern-texas-gulf-coast-cutting-power-to-almost-18-mil
